1|Upgrading to newer releases
2|===========================
3|
4|This section documents migration paths to new releases.
5|
6|.. _upgrading_4_0:
7|
8|Upgrading to 4.0
9|++++++++++++++++
10|
11|``Field`` as a generic class
12|****************************
13|
14|`Field <marshmallow.fields.Field>` is a generic class with a type argument.
15|When defining a custom field, the type argument should be used to specify the internal type.
16|
17|.. code-block:: python
18|
19|    from marshmallow import fields
20|
21|
22|    class PinCode(fields.Field[list[int]]):
23|        """Field that serializes to a string of numbers and deserializes
24|        to a list of numbers.
25|        """
26|
27|        def _serialize(self, value, attr, obj, **kwargs):
28|            if value is None:
29|                return ""
30|            return "".join(str(d) for d in value)
31|
32|        # The inferred return type is list[int]
33|        def _deserialize(self, value, attr, data, **kwargs):
34|            try:
35|                return [int(c) for c in value]
36|            except ValueError as error:
37|                raise ValidationError("Pin codes must contain only digits.") from error
38|
39|New context API
40|***************
41|
42|Passing context to `Schema <marshmallow.schema.Schema>` classes is removed. Use `contextvars.ContextVar` for passing context to
43|fields, pre-/post-processing methods, and validators instead.
44|
45|marshmallow 4 provides an experimental `Context <marshmallow.experimental.context.Context>`
46|wrapper around `contextvars.ContextVar` that can be used to both set and retrieve context.
47|
48|.. code-block:: python
49|
50|    # 3.x
51|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
52|
53|
54|    class UserSchema(Schema):
55|        name_suffixed = fields.Function(
56|            lambda obj, context: obj["name"] + context["suffix"]
57|        )
58|
59|
60|    user_schema = UserSchema()
61|    user_schema.context = {"suffix": "bar"}
62|    user_schema.dump({"name": "foo"})
63|    # {'name_suffixed': 'foobar'}
64|
65|    # 4.x
66|    import typing
67|
68|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
69|    from marshmallow.experimental.context import Context
70|
71|
72|    class UserContext(typing.TypedDict):
73|        suffix: str
74|
75|
76|    UserSchemaContext = Context[UserContext]
77|
78|
79|    class UserSchema(Schema):
80|        name_suffixed = fields.Function(
81|            lambda obj: obj["name"] + UserSchemaContext.get()["suffix"]
82|        )
83|
84|
85|    with UserSchemaContext({"suffix": "bar"}):
86|        UserSchema().dump({"name": "foo"})
87|        # {'name_suffixed': 'foobar'}
88|
89|See :ref:`using_context` for more information.
90|
91|Implicit field creation is removed
92|**********************************
93|
94|In marshmallow 3, the ``fields`` and ``additional`` class Meta options allowed fields to be implicitly created via introspection of the data being serialized.
95|
96|In marshmallow 4.0, implicit field creation is removed to prevent conflicts with libraries
97|that generate fields dynamically.
98|
99|.. code-block:: python
100|
101|    import datetime as dt
102|    import dataclasses
103|
104|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
105|
106|
107|    @dataclasses.dataclass
108|    class User:
109|        name: str
110|        birthdate: dt.date
111|
112|
113|    # 3.x
114|    class UserSchema(Schema):
115|        class Meta:
116|            fields = ("name", "birthdate")
117|
118|
119|    # 4.x
120|    class UserSchema(Schema):
121|        name = fields.String()
122|        email = fields.Date()
123|
124|
125|To automatically generate schema fields from model classes, consider using a separate library, e.g.
126|`marshmallow-sqlalchemy <https://github.com/marshmallow-code/marshmallow-sqlalchemy>`_ for SQLAlchemy models.
127|
128|.. code-block:: python
129|
130|    from marshmallow_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemySchema, auto_field
131|
132|
133|    class UserSchema(SQLAlchemySchema):
134|        class Meta:
135|            model = Author
136|
137|        name = auto_field()
138|        birthdate = auto_field()
139|
140|`@validates <marshmallow.validates>` accepts multiple field names
141|*****************************************************************
142|
143|The `@validates <marshmallow.validates>` decorator now accepts multiple field names as arguments.
144|Decorated methods receive ``data_key`` as a keyword argument.
145|
146|.. code-block:: python
147|
148|    from marshmallow import fields, Schema, validates
149|
150|
151|    # 3.x
152|    class UserSchema(Schema):
153|        name = fields.Str(required=True)
154|        nickname = fields.Str(required=True)
155|
156|        @validates("name")
157|        def validate_name(self, value: str) -> None:
158|            if len(value) < 3:
159|                raise ValidationError('"name" too short')
160|
161|        @validates("nickname")
162|        def validate_nickname(self, value: str) -> None:
163|            if len(value) < 3:
164|                raise ValidationError('"nickname" too short')
165|
166|
167|    # 4.x
168|    class UserSchema(Schema):
169|        name = fields.Str(required=True)
170|        nickname = fields.Str(required=True)
171|
172|        @validates("name", "nickname")
173|        def validate_names(self, value: str, data_key: str) -> None:
174|            if len(value) < 3:
175|                raise ValidationError(f'"{data_key}" too short')
176|
177|
178|Remove ``ordered`` from the `SchemaOpts <marshmallow.SchemaOpts>` constructor
179|*****************************************************************************
180|
181|Subclasses of `marshmallow.SchemaOpts` should remove the ``ordered`` argument from the constructor.
182|
183|.. code-block:: python
184|
185|    # 3.x
186|    class CustomOpts(SchemaOpts):
187|        def __init__(self, meta, ordered=False):
188|            super().__init__(meta, ordered=ordered)
189|            self.custom_option = getattr(meta, "custom_option", False)
190|
191|
192|    # 4.x
193|    class CustomOpts(SchemaOpts):
194|        def __init__(self, meta):
195|            super().__init__(meta)
196|            self.custom_option = getattr(meta, "custom_option", False)
197|
198|``TimeDelta`` changes
199|*********************
200|
201|The `TimeDelta <marshmallow.fields.TimeDelta>` field now preserves float values such that
202|microseconds are included in the resulting `datetime.timedelta` object.
203|
204|.. code-block:: python
205|
206|    from marshmallow import fields
207|
208|    field = fields.TimeDelta()
209|    value = field.deserialize(12.9)
210|
211|    # 3.x
212|    print(value)  # => datetime.timedelta(seconds=12)
213|
214|    # 4.x
215|    print(value)  # => datetime.timedelta(seconds=12, microseconds=900000)
216|
217|The ``serialization_type`` parameter has been removed. Use a custom field or cast the serialized value
218|if you need to change the final output type.
219|
220|``pass_many`` is renamed to ``pass_collection`` in decorators
221|*************************************************************
222|
223|The ``pass_many`` argument to `pre_load <marshmallow.decorators.pre_load>`,
224|`post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>`, `pre_dump <marshmallow.decorators.pre_dump>`,
225|and `post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>` is renamed to ``pass_collection``.
226|
227|The behavior is unchanged.
228|
229|.. code-block:: python
230|
231|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, post_load
232|
233|
234|    # 3.x
235|    class MySchema(Schema):
236|        name = fields.Str()
237|
238|        @post_dump(pass_many=True)
239|        def post_dump(self, data, many, **kwargs): ...
240|
241|
242|    # 4.x
243|    class MySchema(Schema):
244|        name = fields.Str()
245|
246|        @post_dump(pass_collection=True)
247|        def post_dump(self, data, many, **kwargs): ...
248|
249|Rename ``schema`` to ``parent`` in ``_bind_to_schema``
250|******************************************************
251|
252|Custom fields that define a `_bind_to_schema <marshmallow.Fields._bind_to_schema>` method should rename the `schema` argument to `parent`.
253|
254|.. code-block:: python
255|
256|    from marshmallow import fields
257|
258|
259|    # 3.x
260|    class MyField(fields.Field):
261|        def _bind_to_schema(self, field_name: str, schema: Schema | Field): ...
262|
263|
264|    # 4.x
265|    class MyField(fields.Field[int]):
266|        def _bind_to_schema(self, field_name: str, parent: Schema | Field): ...
267|
268|Use standard library functions to handle RFC 822 and ISO 8601 dates, times, and datetimes
269|*****************************************************************************************
270|
271|ISO 8601 and RFC 822 utilities are removed from `marshmallow.utils` in favor
272|of using the standard library implementations.
273|
274|.. code-block:: python
275|
276|    # 3.x
277|    import datetime as dt
278|    from marshmallow.utils import (
279|        from_iso_date,
280|        from_iso_time,
281|        from_iso_datetime,
282|        to_iso_date,
283|        to_iso_time,
284|        isoformat,
285|        from_rfc,
286|        rfc_format,
287|    )
288|
289|    from_iso_date("2013-11-10")
290|    from_iso_time("01:23:45")
291|    from_iso_datetime("2013-11-10T01:23:45")
292|    to_iso_date(dt.date(2013, 11, 10))
293|    to_iso_time(dt.time(1, 23, 45))
294|    isoformat(dt.datetime(2013, 11, 10, 1, 23, 45))
295|    from_rfc("Sun, 10 Nov 2013 01:23:45 -0000")
296|    rfc_format(dt.datetime(2013, 11, 10, 1, 23, 45))
297|
298|    # 4.x
299|    import datetime as dt
300|    import email.utils
301|
302|    dt.date.fromisoformat("2013-11-10")
303|    dt.time.fromisoformat("01:23:45")
304|    dt.datetime.fromisoformat("2013-11-10T01:23:45")
305|    dt.date(2013, 11, 10).isoformat()
306|    dt.time(1, 23, 45).isoformat()
307|    dt.datetime(2013, 11, 10, 1, 23, 45).isoformat()
308|    email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime("Sun, 10 Nov 2013 01:23:45 -0000")
309|    email.utils.format_datetime(dt.datetime(2013, 11, 10, 1, 23, 45))
310|
311|Upgrading to 3.26
312|+++++++++++++++++
313|
314|``ordered`` is deprecated
315|*************************
316|
317|The `ordered <marshmallow.schema.Schema.Meta>` class Meta option is removed, since order is already preserved by default.
318|
319|.. code-block:: python
320|
321|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
322|
323|
324|    # <3.26
325|    class MySchema(Schema):
326|        id = fields.Integer()
327|
328|        class Meta:
329|            ordered = True
330|
331|
332|    # >=3.26
333|    class MySchema(Schema):
334|        id = fields.Integer()
335|
336|.. note::
337|
338|    You can set `marshmallow.Schema.dict_class` to `collections.OrderedDict` to
339|    force the output type of `marshmallow.Schema.dump` to be an `OrderedDict <collections.OrderedDict>`.
340|
341|Upgrading to 3.24
342|+++++++++++++++++
343|
344|``Field`` usage
345|***************
346|
347|`Field <marshmallow.fields.Field>` is the base class for all fields and should not be used directly within schemas.
348|Only use subclasses of `Field <marshmallow.fields.Field>` in your schemas.
349|Instantiating `Field <marshmallow.fields.Field>` will raise a warning in marshmallow>=3.24 and an error in marshmallow 4.0.
350|
351|.. code-block:: python
352|
353|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
354|
355|
356|    # <3.24
357|    class UserSchema(Schema):
358|        name = fields.Field()
359|
360|
361|    # >=3.24
362|    class UserSchema(Schema):
363|        name = fields.String()
364|
365|``Number`` and ``Mapping`` fields as base classes
366|*************************************************
367|
368|`Number <marshmallow.fields.Number>` and `Mapping <marshmallow.fields.Mapping>` are bases classes that should not be used within schemas.
369|Use their subclasses instead.
370|Instantiating `Number <marshmallow.fields.Number>` or `Mapping <marshmallow.fields.Mapping>`
371|will raise a warning in marshmallow>=3.24 and an error in marshmallow 4.0.
372|
373|.. code-block:: python
374|
375|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
376|
377|
378|    # <3.24
379|    class PackageSchema(Schema):
380|        revision = fields.Number()
381|        dependencies = fields.Mapping()
382|
383|
384|    # >=3.24
385|    class PackageSchema(Schema):
386|        revision = fields.Integer()
387|        dependencies = fields.Dict()
388|
389|Validators must raise a :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>`
390|***************************************************************************************
391|
392|Validators must raise a :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>` when the value is invalid.
393|Returning `False` from a validator is deprecated and will be removed in marshmallow 4.0.
394|
395|.. code-block:: python
396|
397|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
398|
399|
400|    # <3.24
401|    class UserSchema(Schema):
402|        password = fields.String(validate=lambda x: x == "password")
403|
404|
405|    # >=3.24
406|    def validate_password(val):
407|        if val != "password":
408|            raise ValidationError("Invalid password.")
409|
410|
411|    class UserSchema(Schema):
412|        password = fields.String(validate=validate_password)
413|
414|
415|If you want to use anonymous functions, you can use this helper function in your code.
416|
417|.. code-block:: python
418|
419|    from typing import Any, Callable
420|
421|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
422|
423|
424|    def predicate(
425|        func: Callable[[Any], bool],
426|    ) -> Callable[[Any], None]:
427|        def validate(value: Any) -> None:
428|            if func(value) is False:
429|                raise ValidationError("Invalid value.")
430|
431|        return validate
432|
433|
434|    # Usage
435|    class UserSchema(Schema):
436|        password = fields.String(validate=predicate(lambda x: x == "password"))
437|
438|``context`` is deprecated
439|*************************
440|
441|Passing ``context`` to `Schema <marshmallow.schema.Schema>` classes will raise a warning in marshmallow>=3.24 and will be removed in marshmallow 4.0. Use `contextvars.ContextVar` for passing context to
442|fields, :doc:`pre-/post-processing methods <marshmallow.decorators>`, and :doc:`validators <marshmallow.validate>` instead.
443|
444|Upgrading to 3.13
445|+++++++++++++++++
446|
447|``load_default`` and ``dump_default``
448|+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
449|
450|The ``missing`` and ``default`` parameters of fields are renamed to
451|``load_default`` and ``dump_default``, respectively.
452|
453|.. code-block:: python
454|
455|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
456|
457|
458|    # < 3.13
459|    class MySchema(Schema):
460|        name = fields.Str(missing="Monty")
461|        age = fields.Int(default=42)
462|
463|
464|    # >=3.13
465|    class MySchema(Schema):
466|        name = fields.Str(load_default="Monty")
467|        age = fields.Int(dump_default=42)
468|
469|``load_default`` and ``dump_default`` are passed to the field constructor as keyword arguments.
470|
471|
472|Upgrading to 3.3
473|++++++++++++++++
474|
475|In 3.3, `fields.Nested <marshmallow.fields.Nested>` may take a callable that returns a schema instance.
476|Use this to resolve order-of-declaration issues when schemas nest each other.
477|
478|.. code-block:: python
479|
480|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
481|
482|
483|    # <3.3
484|    class AlbumSchema(Schema):
485|        title = fields.Str()
486|        artist = fields.Nested("ArtistSchema", only=("name",))
487|
488|
489|    class ArtistSchema(Schema):
490|        name = fields.Str()
491|        albums = fields.List(fields.Nested(AlbumSchema))
492|
493|
494|    # >=3.3
495|    class AlbumSchema(Schema):
496|        title = fields.Str()
497|        artist = fields.Nested(lambda: ArtistSchema(only=("name",)))
498|
499|
500|    class ArtistSchema(Schema):
501|        name = fields.Str()
502|        albums = fields.List(fields.Nested(AlbumSchema))
503|
504|A callable should also be used when nesting a schema within itself.
505|Passing ``"self"`` is deprecated.
506|
507|.. code-block:: python
508|
509|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
510|
511|
512|    # <3.3
513|    class PersonSchema(Schema):
514|        partner = fields.Nested("self", exclude=("partner",))
515|        friends = fields.List(fields.Nested("self"))
516|
517|
518|    # >=3.3
519|    class PersonSchema(Schema):
520|        partner = fields.Nested(lambda: PersonSchema(exclude=("partner")))
521|        friends = fields.List(fields.Nested(lambda: PersonSchema()))
522|
523|.. _upgrading_3_0:
524|
525|Upgrading to 3.0
526|++++++++++++++++
527|
528|Python compatibility
529|********************
530|
531|The marshmallow 3.x series requires Python 3.
532|
533|
534|Schemas are always strict
535|*************************
536|
537|Two major changes were made to (de)serialization behavior:
538|
539|- The ``strict`` parameter was removed. Schemas are always strict.
540|- `Schema().load <marshmallow.Schema.load>` and `Schema().dump <marshmallow.Schema.dump>` don't return a ``(data, errors)`` tuple any more. Only ``data`` is returned.
541|
542|If invalid data are passed, a :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>` is raised.
543|The dictionary of validation errors is accessible from the
544|`ValidationError.messages <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError.messages>` attribute,
545|along with the valid data from the `ValidationError.valid_data
546|<marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError.valid_data>` attribute.
547|
548|.. code-block:: python
549|
550|    from marshmallow import ValidationError
551|
552|    # 2.x
553|    schema = UserSchema()
554|    data, errors = schema.load({"name": "Monty", "email": "monty@python.org"})
555|    # OR
556|    schema = UserSchema(strict=True)
557|    try:
558|        data, _ = schema.load({"name": "Monty", "email": "monty@python.org"})
559|    except ValidationError as err:
560|        errors = err.messages
561|        valid_data = err.valid_data
562|
563|    # 3.x
564|    schema = UserSchema()
565|    # There is only one right way
566|    try:
567|        data = schema.load({"name": "Monty", "email": "monty@python.org"})
568|    except ValidationError as err:
569|        errors = err.messages
570|        valid_data = err.valid_data
571|
572|`Schema.validate <marshmallow.Schema.validate>` always returns a dictionary of validation errors (same as 2.x with ``strict=False``).
573|
574|.. code-block:: python
575|
576|    schema.validate({"email": "invalid"})
577|    # {'email': ['Not a valid email address.']}
578|
579|Setting the ``strict`` option on `class Meta <marshmallow.Schema.Meta>` has no effect on `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` behavior.
580|Passing ``strict=True`` or ``strict=False`` to the `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` constructor
581|will raise a :exc:`TypeError`.
582|
583|
584|.. code-block:: python
585|
586|    # 3.x
587|    UserSchema(strict=True)
588|    # TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'strict'
589|
590|
591|.. seealso::
592|
593|    See GitHub issues :issue:`377` and :issue:`598` for the discussions on
594|    this change.
595|
596|
597|Decorated methods and ``handle_error`` receive ``many`` and ``partial``
598|***********************************************************************
599|
600|Methods decorated with
601|`pre_load <marshmallow.decorators.pre_load>`, `post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>`,
602|`pre_dump <marshmallow.decorators.pre_dump>`, `post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>`,
603|and `validates_schema <marshmallow.decorators.validates_schema>` receive
604|``many`` as a keyword argument. In addition, `pre_load <marshmallow.decorators.pre_load>`, `post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>`,
605|and `validates_schema <marshmallow.decorators.validates_schema>` receive
606|``partial``. To account for these additional arguments, add ``**kwargs`` to your methods.
607|
608|.. code-block:: python
609|
610|    # 2.x
611|    class UserSchema(Schema):
612|        name = fields.Str()
613|        slug = fields.Str()
614|
615|        @pre_load
616|        def slugify_name(self, in_data):
617|            in_data["slug"] = in_data["slug"].lower().strip().replace(" ", "-")
618|            return in_data
619|
620|
621|    # 3.x
622|    class UserSchema(Schema):
623|        name = fields.Str()
624|        slug = fields.Str()
625|
626|        @pre_load
627|        def slugify_name(self, in_data, **kwargs):
628|            in_data["slug"] = in_data["slug"].lower().strip().replace(" ", "-")
629|            return in_data
630|
631|
632|`Schema.handle_error <marshmallow.Schema.handle_error>` also receives ``many`` and ``partial`` as keyword arguments.
633|
634|.. code-block:: python
635|
636|    # 2.x
637|    class UserSchema(Schema):
638|        def handle_error(self, exc, data):
639|            raise AppError("An error occurred with input: {0}".format(data))
640|
641|
642|    # 3.x
643|    class UserSchema(Schema):
644|        def handle_error(self, exc, data, **kwargs):
645|            raise AppError("An error occurred with input: {0}".format(data))
646|
647|
648|Validation does not occur on serialization
649|******************************************
650|
651|`Schema.dump <marshmallow.Schema.dump>` will no longer validate and collect error messages.
652|You *must* ensure your data is valid before serializing it.
653|
654|.. code-block:: python
655|
656|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, ValidationError
657|
658|    invalid_data = dict(created_at="invalid")
659|
660|
661|    class WidgetSchema(Schema):
662|        created_at = fields.DateTime()
663|
664|
665|    # 2.x
666|    WidgetSchema(strict=True).dump(invalid_data)
667|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'created_at': ['"invalid" cannot be formatted as a datetime.']}
668|
669|    # 3.x
670|    WidgetSchema().dump(invalid_data)
671|    # AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'isoformat'
672|
673|
674|Deserializing invalid types raises a ``ValidationError``
675|********************************************************
676|
677|Numbers, booleans, strings, and ``None`` are
678|considered invalid input to `Schema.load
679|<marshmallow.Schema.load>`.
680|
681|.. code-block:: python
682|
683|    # 2.x
684|    # Passes silently
685|    schema.load(None)
686|    schema.load(False)
687|    schema.load("pass")
688|
689|    # 3.x
690|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'_schema': ['Invalid input type.']}
691|    schema.load(None)
692|    schema.load(False)
693|    schema.load("nope")
694|
695|
696|When ``many=True``, non-collection types are also considered invalid.
697|
698|
699|.. code-block:: python
700|
701|    # 2.x
702|    # Passes silently
703|    schema.load(None, many=True)
704|    schema.load({}, many=True)
705|    schema.load("pass", many=True)
706|
707|    # 3.x
708|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'_schema': ['Invalid input type.']}
709|    schema.load(None, many=True)
710|    schema.load({}, many=True)
711|    schema.load("invalid", many=True)
712|
713|
714|``ValidationError.fields`` is removed
715|*************************************
716|
717|:exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>` no
718|longer stores a list of `Field <marshmallow.fields.Field>` instances
719|associated with the validation errors.
720|
721|If you need field instances associated with an error, you can access
722|them from ``schema.fields``.
723|
724|.. code-block:: python
725|
726|
727|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, ValidationError
728|
729|
730|    class MySchema(Schema):
731|        foo = fields.Int()
732|
733|
734|    schema = MySchema()
735|
736|    try:
737|        schema.load({"foo": "invalid"})
738|    except ValidationError as error:
739|        field = schema.fields["foo"]
740|        # ...
741|
742|
743|``ValidationError`` expects a single field name
744|***********************************************
745|
746|:exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>` no
747|longer accepts a list of field names. It expects a single field name. If none
748|is passed, the error refers to the schema.
749|
750|To return an error for several fields at once, a `dict` must be used.
751|
752|.. code-block:: python
753|
754|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, validates_schema, ValidationError
755|
756|
757|    class NumberSchema(Schema):
758|        field_a = fields.Integer()
759|        field_b = fields.Integer()
760|
761|        # 2.x
762|        @validates_schema
763|        def validate_numbers(self, data):
764|            if data["field_b"] >= data["field_a"]:
765|                raise ValidationError(
766|                    "field_a must be greater than field_b", ["field_a", "field_b"]
767|                )
768|
769|        # 3.x
770|        @validates_schema
771|        def validate_numbers(self, data):
772|            if data["field_b"] >= data["field_a"]:
773|                raise ValidationError(
774|                    {
775|                        "field_a": ["field_a must be greater than field_b"],
776|                        "field_b": ["field_a must be greater than field_b"],
777|                    }
778|                )
779|
780|``ValidationError`` error messages are deep-merged
781|**************************************************
782|
783|When multiple :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>`
784|are raised, the error structures are merged in the final :exc:`ValidationError`
785|raised at the end of the process.
786|
787|When reporting error messages as `dict`, the keys should refer to subitems
788|of the item the message refers to, and the values should be error messages.
789|
790|See :doc:`extending/schema_validation` for an example.
791|page for an example.
792|
793|Schemas raise ``ValidationError`` when deserializing data with unknown keys
794|***************************************************************************
795|
796|marshmallow 3.x schemas can deal with unknown keys in three different ways,
797|configurable with the ``unknown`` option:
798|
799|- ``EXCLUDE``: drop those keys (same as marshmallow 2)
800|- ``INCLUDE``: pass those keys/values as is, with no validation performed
801|- ``RAISE`` (default): raise a ``ValidationError``
802|
803|The ``unknown`` option can be passed as a Meta option, on Schema instantiation,
804|or at load time.
805|
806|.. code-block:: python
807|
808|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, EXCLUDE, INCLUDE, RAISE
809|
810|
811|    class MySchema(Schema):
812|        foo = fields.Int()
813|
814|        class Meta:
815|            # Pass EXCLUDE as Meta option to keep marshmallow 2 behavior
816|            unknown = EXCLUDE
817|
818|
819|    MySchema().load({"foo": 42, "bar": "whatever"})  # => ['foo': 42]
820|
821|    #  Value passed on instantiation overrides Meta option
822|    schema = MySchema(unknown=INCLUDE)
823|    schema.load({"foo": 42, "bar": "whatever"})  # => ['foo': 42, 'bar': 'whatever']
824|
825|    #  Value passed on load overrides instance attribute
826|    schema.load({"foo": 42, "bar": "whatever"}, unknown=RAISE)  # => ValidationError
827|
828|Overriding ``get_attribute``
829|****************************
830|
831|If your `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` overrides `get_attribute <marshmallow.Schema.get_attribute>`, you will need to update the method's signature. The positions of the ``attr`` and ``obj`` arguments were switched for consistency with Python builtins, e.g. `getattr`.
832|
833|.. code-block:: python
834|
835|    from marshmallow import Schema
836|
837|
838|    # 2.x
839|    class MySchema(Schema):
840|        def get_attribute(self, attr, obj, default):
841|            return getattr(obj, attr, default)
842|
843|
844|    # 3.x
845|    class MySchema(Schema):
846|        def get_attribute(self, obj, attr, default):
847|            return getattr(obj, attr, default)
848|
849|``pass_original=True`` passes individual items when ``many=True``
850|*****************************************************************
851|
852|When ``pass_original=True`` is passed to
853|`validates_schema <marshmallow.decorators.validates_schema>`,
854|`post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>`, or
855|`post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>`, the `original_data`
856|argument will be a single item corresponding to the (de)serialized
857|datum.
858|
859|.. code-block:: python
860|
861|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, post_load, EXCLUDE
862|
863|
864|    class ShoeSchema(Schema):
865|        size = fields.Int()
866|
867|        class Meta:
868|            unknown = EXCLUDE
869|
870|        @post_load(pass_original=True)
871|        def post_load(self, data, original_data, **kwargs):
872|            # original_data has 'width' but
873|            # data does not because it's not
874|            # in the schema
875|            assert "width" in original_data
876|            assert "width" not in data
877|            return data
878|
879|
880|    input_data = [{"size": 10, "width": "M"}, {"size": 6, "width": "W"}]
881|
882|    print(ShoeSchema(many=True).load(input_data))
883|    # [{'size': 10}, {'size': 6}]
884|
885|
886|``utils.get_func_args`` no longer returns bound arguments
887|*********************************************************
888|
889|The `utils.get_func_args <marshmallow.utils.get_func_args>` function will no longer return bound arguments, e.g. `'self'`.
890|
891|.. code-block:: python
892|
893|    from marshmallow.utils import get_func_args
894|
895|
896|    class MyCallable:
897|        def __call__(self, foo, bar):
898|            return 42
899|
900|
901|    callable_obj = MyCallable()
902|
903|    # 2.x
904|    get_func_args(callable_obj)  # => ['self', 'foo', 'bar']
905|
906|    # 3.x
907|    get_func_args(callable_obj)  # => ['foo', 'bar']
908|
909|
910|Handling ``AttributeError`` in ``Method`` and ``Function`` fields
911|*****************************************************************
912|
913|The `Method <marshmallow.fields.Method>` and `Function <marshmallow.fields.Function>` fields no longer swallow ``AttributeErrors``. Therefore, your methods and functions are responsible for handling inputs such as `None`.
914|
915|.. code-block:: python
916|
917|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, missing
918|
919|
920|    # 2.x
921|    class ShapeSchema(Schema):
922|        area = fields.Method("get_area")
923|
924|        def get_area(self, obj):
925|            return obj.height * obj.length
926|
927|
928|    schema = ShapeSchema()
929|    # In 2.x, the following would pass without errors
930|    # In 3.x, and AttributeError would be raised
931|    result = schema.dump(None)
932|    result  # => {}
933|
934|
935|    # 3.x
936|    class ShapeSchema(Schema):
937|        area = fields.Method("get_area")
938|
939|        def get_area(self, obj):
940|            if obj is None:
941|                # 'area' will not appear in serialized output
942|                return missing
943|            return obj.height * obj.length
944|
945|
946|    schema = ShapeSchema()
947|    result = schema.dump(None)
948|    result  # => {}
949|
950|Adding additional data to serialized output
951|*******************************************
952|
953|Use a `post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>` to add additional data on serialization. The ``extra`` argument on `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` was removed.
954|
955|
956|.. code-block:: python
957|
958|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, post_dump
959|
960|
961|    # 2.x
962|    class MySchema(Schema):
963|        x = fields.Int()
964|        y = fields.Int()
965|
966|
967|    schema = MySchema(extra={"z": 123})
968|    schema.dump({"x": 1, "y": 2})
969|    # => {'z': 123, 'y': 2, 'x': 1}
970|
971|
972|    # 3.x
973|    class MySchema(Schema):
974|        x = fields.Int()
975|        y = fields.Int()
976|
977|        @post_dump
978|        def add_z(self, output):
979|            output["z"] = 123
980|            return output
981|
982|
983|    schema = MySchema()
984|    schema.dump({"x": 1, "y": 2})
985|    # => {'z': 123, 'y': 2, 'x': 1}
986|
987|
988|Schema-level validators are skipped when field validation fails
989|***************************************************************
990|
991|By default, schema validator methods decorated by `validates_schema <marshmallow.decorators.validates_schema>` won't execute if any of the field validators fails (including ``required=True`` validation).
992|
993|.. code-block:: python
994|
995|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, validates_schema, ValidationError
996|
997|
998|    class MySchema(Schema):
999|        x = fields.Int(required=True)
1000|        y = fields.Int(required=True)
1001|
1002|        @validates_schema
1003|        def validate_schema(self, data):
1004|            if data["x"] <= data["y"]:
1005|                raise ValidationError("x must be greater than y")
1006|
1007|
1008|    schema = MySchema()
1009|
1010|    # 2.x
1011|    # A KeyError is raised in validate_schema
1012|    schema.load({"x": 2})
1013|
1014|    # 3.x
1015|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'y': ['Missing data for required field.']}
1016|    # validate_schema is not run
1017|    schema.load({"x": 2})
1018|
1019|If you want a schema validator to run even if a field validator fails, pass ``skip_on_field_errors=False``. Make sure your code handles cases where fields are missing from the deserialized data (due to validation errors).
1020|
1021|
1022|.. code-block:: python
1023|
1024|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, validates_schema, ValidationError
1025|
1026|
1027|    class MySchema(Schema):
1028|        x = fields.Int(required=True)
1029|        y = fields.Int(required=True)
1030|
1031|        @validates_schema(skip_on_field_errors=False)
1032|        def validate_schema(self, data):
1033|            if "x" in data and "y" in data:
1034|                if data["x"] <= data["y"]:
1035|                    raise ValidationError("x must be greater than y")
1036|
1037|
1038|    schema = MySchema()
1039|    schema.load({"x": 2})
1040|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'y': ['Missing data for required field.']}
1041|
1042|`SchemaOpts` constructor receives ``ordered`` argument
1043|******************************************************
1044|
1045|Subclasses of `SchemaOpts <marshmallow.SchemaOpts>` receive an additional argument, ``ordered``, which is `True` if the `ordered` option is set to `True` on a Schema or one of its parent classes.
1046|
1047|.. code-block:: python
1048|
1049|    from marshmallow import SchemaOpts
1050|
1051|
1052|    # 2.x
1053|    class CustomOpts(SchemaOpts):
1054|        def __init__(self, meta):
1055|            super().__init__(meta)
1056|            self.custom_option = getattr(meta, "meta", False)
1057|
1058|
1059|    # 3.x
1060|    class CustomOpts(SchemaOpts):
1061|        def __init__(self, meta, ordered=False):
1062|            super().__init__(meta, ordered)
1063|            self.custom_option = getattr(meta, "meta", False)
1064|
1065|`ContainsOnly` accepts empty and duplicate values
1066|*************************************************
1067|
1068|`validate.ContainsOnly <marshmallow.validate.ContainsOnly>` now accepts duplicate values in the input value.
1069|
1070|
1071|.. code-block:: python
1072|
1073|    from marshmallow import validate
1074|
1075|    validator = validate.ContainsOnly(["red", "blue"])
1076|
1077|    # in 2.x the following raises a ValidationError
1078|    # in 3.x, no error is raised
1079|    validator(["red", "red", "blue"])
1080|
1081|
1082|If you don't want to accept duplicates, use a custom validator, like the following.
1083|
1084|.. code-block:: python
1085|
1086|    from marshmallow import ValidationError
1087|    from marshmallow.validate import ContainsOnly
1088|
1089|
1090|    class ContainsOnlyNoDuplicates(ContainsOnly):
1091|        def __call__(self, value):
1092|            ret = super(ContainsOnlyNoDuplicates, self).__call__(value)
1093|            if len(set(value)) != len(value):
1094|                raise ValidationError("Duplicate values not allowed")
1095|            return ret
1096|
1097|.. note::
1098|
1099|    If you need to handle unhashable types, you can use the  `implementation of
1100|    ContainsOnly from marshmallow 2.x <https://github.com/marshmallow-code/marshmallow/blob/2888e6978bc8c409a5fed35da6ece8bdb23384f2/marshmallow/validate.py#L436-L467>`_.
1101|
1102|`validate.ContainsOnly <marshmallow.validate.ContainsOnly>` also accepts empty values as valid input.
1103|
1104|.. code-block:: python
1105|
1106|    from marshmallow import validate
1107|
1108|    validator = validate.ContainsOnly(["red", "blue"])
1109|
1110|    # in 2.x the following raises a ValidationError
1111|    # in 3.x, no error is raised
1112|    validator([])
1113|
1114|To validate against empty inputs, use `validate.Length(min=1) <marshmallow.validate.Length>`.
1115|
1116|
1117|``json_module`` option is renamed to ``render_module``
1118|******************************************************
1119|
1120|The ``json_module`` `class Meta <marshmallow.Schema.Meta>` option is deprecated in favor of ``render_module``.
1121|
1122|.. code-block:: python
1123|
1124|    import ujson
1125|
1126|
1127|    # 2.x
1128|    class MySchema(Schema):
1129|        class Meta:
1130|            json_module = ujson
1131|
1132|
1133|    # 3.x
1134|    class MySchema(Schema):
1135|        class Meta:
1136|            render_module = ujson
1137|
1138|
1139|``missing`` and ``default`` ``Field`` parameters are passed in deserialized form
1140|********************************************************************************
1141|
1142|.. code-block:: python
1143|
1144|    # 2.x
1145|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1146|        id = fields.UUID(missing=lambda: str(uuid.uuid1()))
1147|        birthdate = fields.DateTime(default=lambda: dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19).isoformat())
1148|
1149|
1150|    # 3.x
1151|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1152|        id = fields.UUID(missing=uuid.uuid1)
1153|        birthdate = fields.DateTime(default=dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19))
1154|
1155|
1156|Pass ``default`` as a keyword argument
1157|**************************************
1158|
1159|`fields.Boolean <marshmallow.fields.Boolean>` now receives additional ``truthy`` and ``falsy`` parameters. Consequently, the ``default`` parameter should always be passed as a keyword argument.
1160|
1161|
1162|.. code-block:: python
1163|
1164|    # 2.x
1165|    fields.Boolean(True)
1166|
1167|    # 3.x
1168|    fields.Boolean(default=True)
1169|
1170|
1171|``Email`` and ``URL`` fields do not validate on serialization
1172|*************************************************************
1173|
1174|`fields.Email <marshmallow.fields.Email>` and `fields.URL <marshmallow.fields.URL>` only validate input upon
1175|deserialization. They do not validate on serialization. This makes them
1176|more consistent with the other fields and improves serialization
1177|performance.
1178|
1179|
1180|``load_from`` and ``dump_to`` are merged into ``data_key``
1181|**********************************************************
1182|
1183|The same key is used for serialization and deserialization.
1184|
1185|.. code-block:: python
1186|
1187|    # 2.x
1188|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1189|        email = fields.Email(load_from="CamelCasedEmail", dump_to="CamelCasedEmail")
1190|
1191|
1192|    # 3.x
1193|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1194|        email = fields.Email(data_key="CamelCasedEmail")
1195|
1196|It is not possible to specify a different key for serialization and deserialization on the same field.
1197|This use case is covered by using two different `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>`.
1198|
1199|.. code-block:: python
1200|
1201|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
1202|
1203|
1204|    # 2.x
1205|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1206|        id = fields.Str()
1207|        email = fields.Email(load_from="CamelCasedEmail", dump_to="snake_case_email")
1208|
1209|
1210|    # 3.x
1211|    class BaseUserSchema(Schema):
1212|        id = fields.Str()
1213|
1214|
1215|    class LoadUserSchema(BaseUserSchema):
1216|        email = fields.Email(data_key="CamelCasedEmail")
1217|
1218|
1219|    class DumpUserSchema(BaseUserSchema):
1220|        email = fields.Email(data_key="snake_case_email")
1221|
1222|
1223|Also, when ``data_key`` is specified on a field, only ``data_key`` is checked in the input data. In marshmallow 2.x the field name is checked if ``load_from`` is missing from the input data.
1224|
1225|Pre/Post-processors must return modified data
1226|*********************************************
1227|
1228|In marshmallow 2.x, ``None`` returned by a pre or post-processor is interpreted as "the data was mutated". In marshmallow 3.x, the return value is considered as processed data even if it is ``None``.
1229|
1230|Processors that mutate the data should be updated to also return it.
1231|
1232|
1233|.. code-block:: python
1234|
1235|    # 2.x
1236|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1237|        name = fields.Str()
1238|        slug = fields.Str()
1239|
1240|        @pre_load
1241|        def slugify_name(self, in_data):
1242|            # In 2.x, implicitly returning None implied that data were mutated
1243|            in_data["slug"] = in_data["slug"].lower().strip().replace(" ", "-")
1244|
1245|
1246|    # 3.x
1247|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1248|        name = fields.Str()
1249|        slug = fields.Str()
1250|
1251|        @pre_load
1252|        def slugify_name(self, in_data, **kwargs):
1253|            # In 3.x, always return the processed data
1254|            in_data["slug"] = in_data["slug"].lower().strip().replace(" ", "-")
1255|            return in_data
1256|
1257|``Nested`` field no longer supports plucking
1258|********************************************
1259|
1260|In marshmallow 2.x, when a string was passed to a ``Nested`` field's ```only`` parameter, the field would be plucked. In marshmallow 3.x, the ``Pluck`` field must be used instead.
1261|
1262|
1263|.. code-block:: python
1264|
1265|    # 2.x
1266|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1267|        name = fields.Str()
1268|        friends = fields.Nested("self", many=True, only="name")
1269|
1270|
1271|    # 3.x
1272|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1273|        name = fields.Str()
1274|        friends = fields.Pluck("self", "name", many=True)
1275|
1276|
1277|Accessing attributes on objects within a list
1278|*********************************************
1279|
1280|In order to serialize attributes on inner objects within a list, use the
1281|``Pluck`` field.
1282|
1283|.. code-block:: python
1284|
1285|    # 2.x
1286|    class FactorySchema(Schema):
1287|        widget_ids = fields.List(fields.Int(attribute="id"))
1288|
1289|
1290|    # 3.x
1291|    class FactorySchema(Schema):
1292|        widget_ids = fields.List(fields.Pluck(WidgetSchema, "id"))
1293|
1294|
1295|``List`` does not wrap single values in a list on serialization
1296|***************************************************************
1297|
1298|In marshmallow 2.x, ``List`` serializes a single object as a list with a single
1299|element. In marshmallow 3.x, the object is assumed to be iterable and passing a
1300|non-iterable element results in an error.
1301|
1302|.. code-block:: python
1303|
1304|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1305|        numbers = fields.List(fields.Int())
1306|
1307|
1308|    user = {"numbers": 1}
1309|    UserSchema().dump(user)
1310|
1311|    # 2.x
1312|    # => {'numbers': [1]}
1313|
1314|    # 3.x
1315|    # => TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable
1316|
1317|
1318|``Float`` field takes a new ``allow_nan`` parameter
1319|***************************************************
1320|
1321|In marshmallow 2.x, ``Float`` field would serialize and deserialize special values such as ``nan``, ``inf`` or ``-inf``. In marshmallow 3, those values trigger a ``ValidationError`` unless ``allow_nan`` is ``True``. ``allow_nan`` defaults to ``False``.
1322|
1323|
1324|.. code-block:: python
1325|
1326|    # 2.x
1327|    class MySchema(Schema):
1328|        x = fields.Float()
1329|
1330|
1331|    MySchema().load({"x": "nan"})
1332|    # => {{'x': nan}}
1333|
1334|
1335|    # 3.x
1336|    class MySchema(Schema):
1337|        x = fields.Float()
1338|        y = fields.Float(allow_nan=True)
1339|
1340|
1341|    MySchema().load({"x": 12, "y": "nan"})
1342|    # => {{'x': 12.0, 'y': nan}}
1343|
1344|    MySchema().load({"x": "nan"})
1345|    # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'x': ['Special numeric values (nan or infinity) are not permitted.']}
1346|
1347|``DateTime`` field ``dateformat`` ``Meta`` option is renamed ``datetimeformat``
1348|*******************************************************************************
1349|
1350|The ``Meta`` option ``dateformat`` used to pass format to `DateTime <marshmallow.fields.DateTime>` field is renamed as ``datetimeformat``.
1351|
1352|`Date <marshmallow.fields.Date>` field gets a new ``format`` parameter to specify the format to use for serialization. ``dateformat`` ``Meta`` option now applies to `Date <marshmallow.fields.Date>` field.
1353|
1354|.. code-block:: python
1355|
1356|    # 2.x
1357|    class MySchema(Schema):
1358|        x = fields.DateTime()
1359|
1360|        class Meta:
1361|            dateformat = "%Y-%m"
1362|
1363|
1364|    MySchema().dump({"x": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19)})
1365|    # => {{'x': '2017-09'}}
1366|
1367|
1368|    # 3.x
1369|    class MySchema(Schema):
1370|        x = fields.DateTime()
1371|        y = fields.Date()
1372|
1373|        class Meta:
1374|            datetimeformat = "%Y-%m"
1375|            dateformat = "%m-%d"
1376|
1377|
1378|    MySchema().dump({"x": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19), "y": dt.date(2017, 9, 19)})
1379|    # => {{'x': '2017-09', 'y': '09-19'}}
1380|
1381|``DateTime`` leaves timezone information untouched during serialization
1382|***********************************************************************
1383|
1384|``DateTime`` does not convert naive datetimes to UTC on serialization and
1385|``LocalDateTime`` is removed.
1386|
1387|.. code-block:: python
1388|
1389|    # 2.x
1390|    class MySchema(Schema):
1391|        x = fields.DateTime()
1392|        y = fields.DateTime()
1393|        z = fields.LocalDateTime()
1394|
1395|
1396|    MySchema().dump(
1397|        {
1398|            "x": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19),
1399|            "y": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19, tzinfo=dt.timezone(dt.timedelta(hours=2))),
1400|            "z": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19, tzinfo=dt.timezone(dt.timedelta(hours=2))),
1401|        }
1402|    )
1403|    # => {{'x': '2017-09-19T00:00:00+00:00', 'y': '2017-09-18T22:00:00+00:00', 'z': '2017-09-19T00:00:00+02:00'}}
1404|
1405|
1406|    # 3.x
1407|    class MySchema(Schema):
1408|        x = fields.DateTime()
1409|        y = fields.DateTime()
1410|
1411|
1412|    MySchema().dump(
1413|        {
1414|            "x": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19),
1415|            "y": dt.datetime(2017, 9, 19, tzinfo=dt.timezone(dt.timedelta(hours=2))),
1416|        }
1417|    )
1418|    # => {{'x': '2017-09-19T00:00:00', 'y': '2017-09-19T00:00:00+02:00'}}
1419|
1420|The ``prefix`` ``Schema`` parameter is removed
1421|**********************************************
1422|
1423|The ``prefix`` parameter of ``Schema`` is removed. The same feature can be achieved using a post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>` method.
1424|
1425|
1426|.. code-block:: python
1427|
1428|    # 2.x
1429|    class MySchema(Schema):
1430|        f1 = fields.Raw()
1431|        f2 = fields.Raw()
1432|
1433|
1434|    MySchema(prefix="pre_").dump({"f1": "one", "f2": "two"})
1435|    # {'pre_f1': 'one', '_pre_f2': 'two'}
1436|
1437|
1438|    # 3.x
1439|    class MySchema(Schema):
1440|        f1 = fields.Raw()
1441|        f2 = fields.Raw()
1442|
1443|        @post_dump
1444|        def prefix_usr(self, data):
1445|            return {"usr_{}".format(k): v for k, v in iteritems(data)}
1446|
1447|
1448|    MySchema().dump({"f1": "one", "f2": "two"})
1449|    # {'pre_f1': 'one', '_pre_f2': 'two'}
1450|
1451|
1452|``fields.FormattedString`` is removed
1453|*************************************
1454|
1455|``fields.FormattedString`` field is removed. Use `fields.Function
1456|<marshmallow.fields.Function>` or
1457|`fields.Method <marshmallow.fields.Method>` instead.
1458|
1459|.. code-block:: python
1460|
1461|    # 2.x
1462|    class MySchema(Schema):
1463|        full_name = fields.FormattedString("{first_name} {last_name}")
1464|
1465|
1466|    # 3.x
1467|    class MySchema(Schema):
1468|        full_name = fields.Function(lambda u: f"{u.first_name} {u.last_name}")
1469|
1470|
1471|``attribute`` or ``data_key`` collision triggers an exception
1472|*************************************************************
1473|
1474|When a `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` is instantiated, a check is performed and a ``ValueError`` is triggered if
1475|
1476|- several fields have the same ``attribute`` value (or field name if ``attribute`` is not passed), excluding ``dump_only`` fields, or
1477|- several fields have the same ``data_key`` value (or field name if ``data_key`` is not passed), excluding ``load_only`` fields
1478|
1479|In marshmallow 2, it was possible to have multiple fields with the same ``attribute``. It would work provided the ``Schema`` was only used for dumping. When loading, the behaviour was undefined. In marshmallow 3, all but one of those fields must be marked as ``dump_only``. Likewise for ``data_key`` (formerly ``dump_to``) for fields that are not ``load_only``.
1480|
1481|.. code-block:: python
1482|
1483|    # 2.x
1484|    class MySchema(Schema):
1485|        f1 = fields.Raw()
1486|        f2 = fields.Raw(attribute="f1")
1487|        f3 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5")
1488|        f4 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5")
1489|
1490|
1491|    MySchema()
1492|    #  No error
1493|
1494|
1495|    # 3.x
1496|    class MySchema(Schema):
1497|        f1 = fields.Raw()
1498|        f2 = fields.Raw(attribute="f1")
1499|        f3 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5")
1500|        f4 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5")
1501|
1502|
1503|    MySchema()
1504|    # ValueError: 'Duplicate attributes: ['f1', 'f5]'
1505|
1506|
1507|    class MySchema(Schema):
1508|        f1 = fields.Raw()
1509|        f2 = fields.Raw(attribute="f1", dump_only=True)
1510|        f3 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5")
1511|        f4 = fields.Raw(attribute="f5", dump_only=True)
1512|
1513|
1514|    MySchema()
1515|    # No error
1516|
1517|
1518|``Field.fail`` is deprecated in favor of ``Field.make_error``
1519|*************************************************************
1520|
1521|`Field.fail <marshmallow.fields.Field.fail>` is deprecated.
1522|Use `Field.make_error <marshmallow.fields.Field.fail>`. This allows you to
1523|re-raise exceptions using ``raise ... from ...``.
1524|
1525|.. code-block:: python
1526|
1527|    from marshmallow import fields, ValidationError
1528|    from packaging import version
1529|
1530|
1531|    # 2.x
1532|    class Version(fields.Field):
1533|        default_error_messages = {"invalid": "Not a valid version."}
1534|
1535|        def _deserialize(self, value, *args, **kwargs):
1536|            try:
1537|                return version.Version(value)
1538|            except version.InvalidVersion:
1539|                self.fail("invalid")
1540|
1541|
1542|    # 3.x
1543|    class Version(fields.Field):
1544|        default_error_messages = {"invalid": "Not a valid version."}
1545|
1546|        def _deserialize(self, value, *args, **kwargs):
1547|            try:
1548|                return version.Version(value)
1549|            except version.InvalidVersion as error:
1550|                raise self.make_error("invalid") from error
1551|
1552|
1553|``python-dateutil`` recommended dependency is removed
1554|*****************************************************
1555|
1556|In marshmallow 2, ``python-dateutil`` was used to deserialize RFC or ISO 8601
1557|datetimes if it was installed. In marshmallow 3, datetime deserialization is
1558|done with no additional dependency.
1559|
1560|``python-dateutil`` is no longer used by marshmallow.
1561|
1562|
1563|Custom Fields
1564|*************
1565|
1566|To make your custom fields compatible with marshmallow 3, ``_deserialize``
1567|should accept ``**kwargs``:
1568|
1569|.. code-block:: python
1570|
1571|    from marshmallow import fields, ValidationError
1572|    from packaging import version
1573|
1574|
1575|    # 2.x
1576|    class MyCustomField(fields.Field):
1577|        def _deserialize(self, value, attr, obj): ...
1578|
1579|
1580|    # 3.x
1581|    class MyCustomField(fields.Field):
1582|        def _deserialize(self, value, attr, obj, **kwargs): ...
1583|
1584|
1585|Upgrading to 2.3
1586|++++++++++++++++
1587|
1588|The ``func`` parameter of `fields.Function <marshmallow.fields.Function>` was renamed to ``serialize``.
1589|
1590|
1591|.. code-block:: python
1592|
1593|    # YES
1594|    lowername = fields.Function(serialize=lambda obj: obj.name.lower())
1595|    # or
1596|    lowername = fields.Function(lambda obj: obj.name.lower())
1597|
1598|    # NO
1599|    lowername = fields.Function(func=lambda obj: obj.name.lower())
1600|
1601|Similarly, the ``method_name`` of `fields.Method <marshmallow.fields.Method>` was also renamed to ``serialize``.
1602|
1603|.. code-block:: python
1604|
1605|    # YES
1606|    lowername = fields.Method(serialize="lowercase")
1607|    # or
1608|    lowername = fields.Method("lowercase")
1609|
1610|    # NO
1611|    lowername = fields.Method(method_name="lowercase")
1612|
1613|The ``func`` parameter is still available for backwards-compatibility. It will be removed in marshmallow 3.0.
1614|
1615|Both `fields.Function <marshmallow.fields.Function>` and `fields.Method <marshmallow.fields.Method>` will allow the serialize parameter to not be passed, in this case use the ``deserialize`` parameter by name.
1616|
1617|.. code-block:: python
1618|
1619|    lowername = fields.Function(deserialize=lambda name: name.lower())
1620|    # or
1621|    lowername = fields.Method(deserialize="lowername")
1622|
1623|Upgrading to 2.0
1624|++++++++++++++++
1625|
1626|Deserializing `None`
1627|********************
1628|
1629|In 2.0, validation/deserialization of `None` is consistent across field types. If ``allow_none`` is `False` (the default), validation fails when the field's value is `None`. If ``allow_none`` is `True`, `None` is considered valid, and the field deserializes to `None`.
1630|
1631|
1632|.. code-block:: python
1633|
1634|    from marshmallow import fields
1635|
1636|    # In 1.0, deserialization of None was inconsistent
1637|    fields.Int().deserialize(None)  # 0
1638|    fields.Str().deserialize(None)  # ''
1639|    fields.DateTime().deserialize(None)  # error: Could not deserialize None to a datetime.
1640|
1641|
1642|    # In 2.0, validation/deserialization of None is consistent
1643|    fields.Int().deserialize(None)  # error: Field may not be null.
1644|    fields.Str().deserialize(None)  # error: Field may not be null.
1645|    fields.DateTime().deserialize(None)  # error: Field may not be null.
1646|
1647|    # allow_none makes None a valid value
1648|    fields.Int(allow_none=True).deserialize(None)  # None
1649|
1650|Default values
1651|**************
1652|
1653|Before version 2.0, certain fields (including `String <marshmallow.fields.String>`, `List <marshmallow.fields.List>`, `Nested <marshmallow.fields.Nested>`, and number fields) had implicit default values that would be used if their corresponding input value was `None` or missing.
1654|
1655|
1656|In 2.0, these implicit defaults are removed.  A `Field's <marshmallow.fields.Field>` ``default`` parameter is only used if you explicitly set it. Otherwise, missing inputs will be excluded from the serialized output.
1657|
1658|.. code-block:: python
1659|
1660|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
1661|
1662|
1663|    class MySchema(Schema):
1664|        str_no_default = fields.Str()
1665|        int_no_default = fields.Int()
1666|        list_no_default = fields.List(fields.Str)
1667|
1668|
1669|    schema = MySchema()
1670|
1671|    # In 1.0, None was treated as a missing input, so implicit default values were used
1672|    schema.dump(
1673|        {"str_no_default": None, "int_no_default": None, "list_no_default": None}
1674|    ).data
1675|    # {'str_no_default': '', 'int_no_default': 0, 'list_no_default': []}
1676|
1677|    # In 2.0, None serializes to None. No more implicit defaults.
1678|    schema.dump(
1679|        {"str_no_default": None, "int_no_default": None, "list_no_default": None}
1680|    ).data
1681|    # {'str_no_default': None, 'int_no_default': None, 'list_no_default': None}
1682|
1683|
1684|.. code-block:: python
1685|
1686|    # In 1.0, implicit default values were used for missing inputs
1687|    schema.dump({}).data
1688|    # {'int_no_default': 0, 'str_no_default': '', 'list_no_default': []}
1689|
1690|    # In 2.0, missing inputs are excluded from the serialized output
1691|    # if no defaults are specified
1692|    schema.dump({}).data
1693|    # {}
1694|
1695|
1696|As a consequence of this new behavior, the ``skip_missing`` `class Meta <marshmallow.Schema.Meta>` option has been removed.
1697|
1698|
1699|Pre-processing and post-processing methods
1700|******************************************
1701|
1702|The pre- and post-processing API was significantly improved for better consistency and flexibility. The `pre_load <marshmallow.decorators.pre_load>`, `post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>`, `pre_dump <marshmallow.decorators.pre_dump>`, and `post_dump <marshmallow.decorators.post_dump>` should be used to define processing hooks. ``Schema.preprocessor`` and ``Schema.data_handler`` are removed.
1703|
1704|
1705|.. code-block:: python
1706|
1707|    # 1.0 API
1708|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
1709|
1710|
1711|    class ExampleSchema(Schema):
1712|        field_a = fields.Int()
1713|
1714|
1715|    @ExampleSchema.preprocessor
1716|    def increment(schema, data):
1717|        data["field_a"] += 1
1718|        return data
1719|
1720|
1721|    @ExampleSchema.data_handler
1722|    def decrement(schema, data, obj):
1723|        data["field_a"] -= 1
1724|        return data
1725|
1726|
1727|    # 2.0 API
1728|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, pre_load, post_dump
1729|
1730|
1731|    class ExampleSchema(Schema):
1732|        field_a = fields.Int()
1733|
1734|        @pre_load
1735|        def increment(self, data):
1736|            data["field_a"] += 1
1737|            return data
1738|
1739|        @post_dump
1740|        def decrement(self, data):
1741|            data["field_a"] -= 1
1742|            return data
1743|
1744|See the :doc:`extending/pre_and_post_processing` page for more information on the ``pre_*`` and ``post_*`` decorators.
1745|
1746|Schema validators
1747|*****************
1748|
1749|Similar to pre-processing and post-processing methods, schema validators are now defined as methods. Decorate schema validators with `validates_schema <marshmallow.decorators.validates_schema>`. ``Schema.validator`` is removed.
1750|
1751|.. code-block:: python
1752|
1753|    # 1.0 API
1754|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, ValidationError
1755|
1756|
1757|    class MySchema(Schema):
1758|        field_a = fields.Int(required=True)
1759|        field_b = fields.Int(required=True)
1760|
1761|
1762|    @ExampleSchema.validator
1763|    def validate_schema(schema, data):
1764|        if data["field_a"] < data["field_b"]:
1765|            raise ValidationError("field_a must be greater than field_b")
1766|
1767|
1768|    # 2.0 API
1769|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, validates_schema, ValidationError
1770|
1771|
1772|    class MySchema(Schema):
1773|        field_a = fields.Int(required=True)
1774|        field_b = fields.Int(required=True)
1775|
1776|        @validates_schema
1777|        def validate_schema(self, data):
1778|            if data["field_a"] < data["field_b"]:
1779|                raise ValidationError("field_a must be greater than field_b")
1780|
1781|Custom accessors and error handlers
1782|***********************************
1783|
1784|Custom accessors and error handlers are now defined as methods. ``Schema.accessor`` and ``Schema.error_handler`` are deprecated.
1785|
1786|.. code-block:: python
1787|
1788|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
1789|
1790|
1791|    # 1.0 Deprecated API
1792|    class ExampleSchema(Schema):
1793|        field_a = fields.Int()
1794|
1795|
1796|    @ExampleSchema.accessor
1797|    def get_from_dict(schema, attr, obj, default=None):
1798|        return obj.get(attr, default)
1799|
1800|
1801|    @ExampleSchema.error_handler
1802|    def handle_errors(schema, errors, obj):
1803|        raise CustomError("Something bad happened", messages=errors)
1804|
1805|
1806|    # 2.0 API
1807|    class ExampleSchema(Schema):
1808|        field_a = fields.Int()
1809|
1810|        def get_attribute(self, attr, obj, default):
1811|            return obj.get(attr, default)
1812|
1813|        # handle_error gets passed a ValidationError
1814|        def handle_error(self, exc, data):
1815|            raise CustomError("Something bad happened", messages=exc.messages)
1816|
1817|Use `post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>` instead of `make_object`
1818|***************************************************************************
1819|
1820|The `make_object` method was deprecated from the `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` API (see :issue:`277` for the rationale). In order to deserialize to an object, use a `post_load <marshmallow.decorators.post_load>` method.
1821|
1822|.. code-block:: python
1823|
1824|    # 1.0
1825|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, post_load
1826|
1827|
1828|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1829|        name = fields.Str()
1830|        created_at = fields.DateTime()
1831|
1832|        def make_object(self, data):
1833|            return User(**data)
1834|
1835|
1836|    # 2.0
1837|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, post_load
1838|
1839|
1840|    class UserSchema(Schema):
1841|        name = fields.Str()
1842|        created_at = fields.DateTime()
1843|
1844|        @post_load
1845|        def make_user(self, data):
1846|            return User(**data)
1847|
1848|Error format when ``many=True``
1849|*******************************
1850|
1851|When validating a collection (i.e. when calling ``load`` or ``dump`` with ``many=True``), the errors dictionary will be keyed on the indices of invalid items.
1852|
1853|.. code-block:: python
1854|
1855|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
1856|
1857|
1858|    class BandMemberSchema(Schema):
1859|        name = fields.String(required=True)
1860|        email = fields.Email()
1861|
1862|
1863|    user_data = [
1864|        {"email": "mick@stones.com", "name": "Mick"},
1865|        {"email": "invalid", "name": "Invalid"},  # invalid email
1866|        {"email": "keith@stones.com", "name": "Keith"},
1867|        {"email": "charlie@stones.com"},  # missing "name"
1868|    ]
1869|
1870|    result = BandMemberSchema(many=True).load(user_data)
1871|
1872|    # 1.0
1873|    result.errors
1874|    # {'email': ['"invalid" is not a valid email address.'],
1875|    #  'name': ['Missing data for required field.']}
1876|
1877|    # 2.0
1878|    result.errors
1879|    # {1: {'email': ['"invalid" is not a valid email address.']},
1880|    #  3: {'name': ['Missing data for required field.']}}
1881|
1882|You can still get the pre-2.0 behavior by setting ``index_errors = False`` in a ``Schema's`` `class Meta <marshmallow.Schema.Meta>` options.
1883|
1884|Use ``ValidationError`` instead of ``MarshallingError`` and ``UnmarshallingError``
1885|**********************************************************************************
1886|
1887|The :exc:`MarshallingError` and :exc:`UnmarshallingError` exceptions are deprecated in favor of a single :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>`. Users who have written custom fields or are using ``strict`` mode will need to change their code accordingly.
1888|
1889|Handle ``ValidationError`` in strict mode
1890|-----------------------------------------
1891|
1892|When using `strict` mode, you should handle `ValidationErrors` when calling `Schema.dump <marshmallow.Schema.dump>` and `Schema.load <marshmallow.Schema.load>`.
1893|
1894|.. code-block:: python
1895|
1896|    from marshmallow import exceptions as exc
1897|
1898|    schema = BandMemberSchema(strict=True)
1899|
1900|    # 1.0
1901|    try:
1902|        schema.load({"email": "invalid-email"})
1903|    except exc.UnmarshallingError as err:
1904|        handle_error(err)
1905|
1906|    # 2.0
1907|    try:
1908|        schema.load({"email": "invalid-email"})
1909|    except exc.ValidationError as err:
1910|        handle_error(err)
1911|
1912|
1913|Accessing error messages in strict mode
1914|***************************************
1915|
1916|In 2.0, `strict` mode was improved so that you can access all error messages for a schema (rather than failing early) by accessing a `ValidationError's` ``messages`` attribute.
1917|
1918|.. code-block:: python
1919|
1920|    schema = BandMemberSchema(strict=True)
1921|
1922|    try:
1923|        result = schema.load({"email": "invalid"})
1924|    except ValidationMessage as err:
1925|        print(err.messages)
1926|    # {
1927|    #     'email': ['"invalid" is not a valid email address.'],
1928|    #     'name': ['Missing data for required field.']
1929|    # }
1930|
1931|
1932|Custom fields
1933|*************
1934|
1935|Two changes must be made to make your custom fields compatible with version 2.0.
1936|
1937|- The `_deserialize <marshmallow.fields.Field._deserialize>` method of custom fields now receives ``attr`` (the key corresponding to the value to be deserialized) and the raw input ``data`` as arguments.
1938|- Custom fields should raise :exc:`ValidationError <marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError>` in their `_deserialize` and `_serialize` methods when a validation error occurs.
1939|
1940|.. code-block:: python
1941|
1942|    from marshmallow import fields, ValidationError
1943|    from marshmallow.exceptions import UnmarshallingError
1944|
1945|
1946|    # In 1.0, an UnmarshallingError was raised
1947|    class PasswordField(fields.Field):
1948|        def _deserialize(self, val):
1949|            if not len(val) >= 6:
1950|                raise UnmarshallingError("Password too short.")
1951|            return val
1952|
1953|
1954|    # In 2.0, _deserialize receives attr and data,
1955|    # and a ValidationError is raised
1956|    class PasswordField(fields.Field):
1957|        def _deserialize(self, val, attr, data):
1958|            if not len(val) >= 6:
1959|                raise ValidationError("Password too short.")
1960|            return val
1961|
1962|
1963|To make a field compatible with both marshmallow 1.x and 2.x, you can pass `*args` and `**kwargs` to the signature.
1964|
1965|.. code-block:: python
1966|
1967|    class PasswordField(fields.Field):
1968|        def _deserialize(self, val, *args, **kwargs):
1969|            if not len(val) >= 6:
1970|                raise ValidationError("Password too short.")
1971|            return val
1972|
1973|Custom error messages
1974|*********************
1975|
1976|Error messages can be customized at the `Field` class or instance level.
1977|
1978|
1979|.. code-block:: python
1980|
1981|    # 1.0
1982|    field = fields.Number(error="You passed a bad number")
1983|
1984|    # 2.0
1985|    # Instance-level
1986|    field = fields.Number(error_messages={"invalid": "You passed a bad number."})
1987|
1988|
1989|    # Class-level
1990|    class MyNumberField(fields.Number):
1991|        default_error_messages = {"invalid": "You passed a bad number."}
1992|
1993|Passing a string to ``required`` is deprecated.
1994|
1995|.. code-block:: python
1996|
1997|    # 1.0
1998|    field = fields.Str(required="Missing required argument.")
1999|
2000|    # 2.0
2001|    field = fields.Str(error_messages={"required": "Missing required argument."})
2002|
2003|
2004|Use ``OneOf`` instead of ``fields.Select``
2005|******************************************
2006|
2007|The `fields.Select` field is deprecated in favor of the newly-added `OneOf` validator.
2008|
2009|.. code-block:: python
2010|
2011|    from marshmallow import fields
2012|    from marshmallow.validate import OneOf
2013|
2014|    # 1.0
2015|    fields.Select(["red", "blue"])
2016|
2017|    # 2.0
2018|    fields.Str(validate=OneOf(["red", "blue"]))
2019|
2020|Accessing context from method fields
2021|************************************
2022|
2023|Use ``self.context`` to access a schema's context within a ``Method`` field.
2024|
2025|.. code-block:: python
2026|
2027|    class UserSchema(Schema):
2028|        name = fields.String()
2029|        likes_bikes = fields.Method("writes_about_bikes")
2030|
2031|        def writes_about_bikes(self, user):
2032|            return "bicycle" in self.context["blog"].title.lower()
2033|
2034|
2035|Validation error messages
2036|*************************
2037|
2038|The default error messages for many fields and validators have been changed for better consistency.
2039|
2040|.. code-block:: python
2041|
2042|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, validate
2043|
2044|
2045|    class ValidatingSchema(Schema):
2046|        foo = fields.Str()
2047|        bar = fields.Bool()
2048|        baz = fields.Int()
2049|        qux = fields.Float()
2050|        spam = fields.Decimal(2, 2)
2051|        eggs = fields.DateTime()
2052|        email = fields.Str(validate=validate.Email())
2053|        homepage = fields.Str(validate=validate.URL())
2054|        nums = fields.List(fields.Int())
2055|
2056|
2057|    schema = ValidatingSchema()
2058|    invalid_data = {
2059|        "foo": 42,
2060|        "bar": 24,
2061|        "baz": "invalid-integer",
2062|        "qux": "invalid-float",
2063|        "spam": "invalid-decimal",
2064|        "eggs": "invalid-datetime",
2065|        "email": "invalid-email",
2066|        "homepage": "invalid-url",
2067|        "nums": "invalid-list",
2068|    }
2069|    errors = schema.validate(invalid_data)
2070|    # {
2071|    #     'foo': ['Not a valid string.'],
2072|    #     'bar': ['Not a valid boolean.'],
2073|    #     'baz': ['Not a valid integer.'],
2074|    #     'qux': ['Not a valid number.'],
2075|    #     'spam': ['Not a valid number.']
2076|    #     'eggs': ['Not a valid datetime.'],
2077|    #     'email': ['Not a valid email address.'],
2078|    #     'homepage': ['Not a valid URL.'],
2079|    #     'nums': ['Not a valid list.'],
2080|    # }
2081|
2082|More
2083|****
2084|
2085|For a full list of changes in 2.0, see the :doc:`changelog <changelog>`.
2086|
2087|
2088|Upgrading to 1.2
2089|++++++++++++++++
2090|
2091|Validators
2092|**********
2093|
2094|Validators were rewritten as class-based callables, making them easier to use when declaring fields.
2095|
2096|.. code-block:: python
2097|
2098|    from marshmallow import fields
2099|
2100|    # 1.2
2101|    from marshmallow.validate import Range
2102|
2103|    age = fields.Int(validate=[Range(min=0, max=999)])
2104|
2105|    # Pre-1.2
2106|    from marshmallow.validate import ranging
2107|
2108|    age = fields.Int(validate=[lambda val: ranging(val, min=0, max=999)])
2109|
2110|
2111|The validator functions from 1.1 are deprecated and will be removed in 2.0.
2112|
2113|Deserializing the empty string
2114|******************************
2115|
2116|
2117|In version 1.2, deserialization of the empty string (``''``) with `DateTime`, `Date`, `Time`, or `TimeDelta` fields results in consistent error messages, regardless of whether or not `python-dateutil` is installed.
2118|
2119|.. code-block:: python
2120|
2121|    from marshmallow import fields
2122|
2123|    fields.Date().deserialize("")
2124|    # UnmarshallingError: Could not deserialize '' to a date object.
2125|
2126|
2127|Decimal
2128|*******
2129|
2130|The `Decimal` field was added to support serialization/deserialization of `decimal.Decimal` numbers. You should use this field when dealing with numbers where precision is critical. The `Fixed`, `Price`, and `Arbitrary` fields are deprecated in favor the `Decimal` field.
2131|
2132|
2133|Upgrading to 1.0
2134|++++++++++++++++
2135|
2136|Version 1.0 marks the first major release of marshmallow. Many big changes were made from the pre-1.0 releases in order to provide a cleaner API, support object deserialization, and improve field validation.
2137|
2138|Perhaps the largest change is in how objects get serialized. Serialization occurs by invoking the :meth:`Schema.dump` method rather than passing the object to the constructor.  Because only configuration options (e.g. the ``many``, ``strict``, and ``only`` parameters) are passed to the constructor, you can more easily reuse serializer instances.  The :meth:`dump <Schema.dump>` method also forms a nice symmetry with the :meth:`Schema.load` method, which is used for deserialization.
2139|
2140|.. code-block:: python
2141|
2142|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields
2143|
2144|
2145|    class UserSchema(Schema):
2146|        email = fields.Email()
2147|        name = fields.String()
2148|
2149|
2150|    user = User(email="monty@python.org", name="Monty Python")
2151|
2152|    # 1.0
2153|    serializer = UserSchema()
2154|    data, errors = serializer.dump(user)
2155|    # OR
2156|    result = serializer.dump(user)
2157|    result.data  # => serialized result
2158|    result.errors  # => errors
2159|
2160|    # Pre-1.0
2161|    serialized = UserSchema(user)
2162|    data = serialized.data
2163|    errors = serialized.errors
2164|
2165|.. note::
2166|
2167|    Some crucial parts of the pre-1.0 API have been retained to ease the transition. You can still pass an object to a `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` constructor and access the `Schema.data` and `Schema.errors` properties. The `is_valid` method, however, has been completely removed. It is recommended that you migrate to the new API to prevent future releases from breaking your code.
2168|
2169|The Fields interface was also reworked in 1.0 to make it easier to define custom fields with their own serialization and deserialization behavior. Custom fields now implement :meth:`Field._serialize` and :meth:`Field._deserialize`.
2170|
2171|.. code-block:: python
2172|
2173|    from marshmallow import fields, MarshallingError
2174|
2175|
2176|    class PasswordField(fields.Field):
2177|        def _serialize(self, value, attr, obj):
2178|            if not value or len(value) < 6:
2179|                raise MarshallingError("Password must be greater than 6 characters.")
2180|            return str(value).strip()
2181|
2182|        # Similarly, you can override the _deserialize method
2183|
2184|Another major change in 1.0 is that multiple validation errors can be stored for a single field. The ``errors`` dictionary returned by :meth:`Schema.dump` and :meth:`Schema.load` is a list of error messages keyed by field name.
2185|
2186|
2187|.. code-block:: python
2188|
2189|    from marshmallow import Schema, fields, ValidationError
2190|
2191|
2192|    def must_have_number(val):
2193|        if not any(ch.isdigit() for ch in val):
2194|            raise ValidationError("Value must have an number.")
2195|
2196|
2197|    def validate_length(val):
2198|        if len(val) < 8:
2199|            raise ValidationError("Value must have 8 or more characters.")
2200|
2201|
2202|    class ValidatingSchema(Schema):
2203|        password = fields.String(validate=[must_have_number, validate_length])
2204|
2205|
2206|    result, errors = ValidatingSchema().load({"password": "secure"})
2207|    print(errors)
2208|    # {'password': ['Value must have an number.',
2209|    #               'Value must have 8 or more characters.']}
2210|
2211|Other notable changes:
2212|
2213|- Serialized output is no longer an ``OrderedDict`` by default. You must explicitly set the `ordered` `class Meta <marshmallow.Schema.Meta>` option to `True` .
2214|- ``Serializer`` has been renamed to `Schema <marshmallow.schema.Schema>`, but you can still import ``marshmallow.Serializer`` (which is aliased to `Schema <marshmallow.Schema>`).
2215|- ``datetime`` objects serialize to ISO8601-formatted strings by default (instead of RFC821 format).
2216|- The ``fields.validated`` decorator was removed, as it is no longer necessary given the new Fields interface.
2217|- ``Schema.factory`` class method was removed.
2218|
2219|.. seealso::
2220|
2221|    See the :doc:`changelog <changelog>` for a more complete listing of added features, bugfixes and breaking changes.
--- END FILE: docs/upgrading.rst ---
